title: Influencer content and copyright - who actually owns it
p1:
You posted the video. You built the audience. You created the idea. But do you actually own the content you made?

Many influencers are surprised to learn the answer is not always as simple as "yes."
p2:
A common belief is that whoever appears in a photo or records a video automatically owns it. The reality is that copyright usually belongs to the person who creates the original work, unless rights were transferred through an agreement.

That means a photographer, editor, agency, or brand could sometimes own parts of the content you helped create.
p3:
Copyright is basically the legal ownership of creative work. For influencers, the safest approach is knowing what your contracts say before signing them. A brand collaboration agreement may allow you to post content while giving the brand permission to reuse it elsewhere.

The creator, the platform, and the business may all have different rights depending on the situation.

A simple rule: creating content does not always mean controlling every use of it.
conclusion: Have you ever created content for a brand or platform without knowing who actually owned the rights? What was your experience?
